aggregation: token-weighted (see kl_prompts docstring: longctx ~58% of tokens)

rows.reference: pipelined engine, hot_set = ALL 32 experts (nothing streamed), same model, same run
rows.test: pipelined engine, hot_set = 16/32 experts pinned in VRAM, remainder streamed from host DRAM (24 layers patched)
rows.scoring: decode-shaped teacher forcing (one token per forward, KV cache) on BOTH sides — not the prefill scorer the other rows use; this engine only engages at T==1
rows.expectation: exactly 0.000 — CONFIRMATORY; where a weight lives must not change the arithmetic performed on it. Same bytes, same GEMM, reached via a different source address: the engine holds the kernel fixed and takes K as data, so only location varies between these two sides.
rows.amendment: Twice-amended, both disclosed. (1) The row could not run at all — enable_pipelined_residency refused ExpertsLoRA bases, which is every model load_moe_4bit_streaming returns. (2) It then scored with the prefill scorer, which engages this decode-only engine zero times and would have reported a flawless 0.000 that measured nothing; scoring is now decode-shaped. A third change was considered and REJECTED on evidence: the 0.000 expectation was briefly withdrawn after the original reference side (a model with NO engine) measured 3.16e-3. That comparison varied weight location AND compute kernel together, so it could not test the row's claim. With the reference moved onto the engine at hot_set=ALL, the kernel is held fixed, and the registered 0.000 is met exactly — see granite-hot-kernel-vs-reference.json for the 3.16e-3, which is the KERNEL's cost and is a separate finding.
rows.witness: the ASYMMETRY is the measurement: the test side must stream (nonzero cold bytes — otherwise nothing was tiered and the engine may not even have run) and the reference side must not (zero — otherwise it is not all-resident and both sides are the same experiment). A 0.000 is only meaningful with both.
